title: Lesson 23 - The Sharing Architecture: OWD, Role Hierarchy, and Sharing Rules
description: Given a set of business requirements, identify the appropriate security model (sharing rules, role hierarchy, Account Teams, Opportunity Teams, permission sets, permission set groups).

questions.question: The Opportunity OWD is Private and a sales manager's role sits above the reps. What does the manager see?
options: Nothing, because Private hides the records from everyone but the owner
The manager sees the reps' opportunities through the role hierarchy
The manager must be added to each opportunity's team
questions.explanation: A Private OWD restricts to the owner and users above them in the role hierarchy, so the manager sees the reports' records without a team or sharing rule.

questions.question: Can a sharing rule remove access from a group that already has it?
options: Yes, if the rule is criteria-based
No, because sharing rules only extend the access the OWD and role hierarchy provide
Yes, when the target is a public group
questions.explanation: Sharing rules are additive only, so removing access requires a change to the OWD, object permissions, or field-level security rather than a sharing rule.

questions.question: Which configuration makes contact visibility follow the account's sharing?
options: Controlled by Parent as the Contact organization-wide default
Grant Access Using Hierarchies cleared on Contact
questions.explanation: Setting the Contact OWD to Controlled by Parent makes contacts inherit their account's access, so no separate contact sharing model is needed.
